question: Should exec denylist policy be persisted in both `openclaw.json` and `exec-approvals.json` with stricter-wins union semantics, or should one surface be the canonical owner?
rationale: This choice defines a permanent privileged-execution policy contract, including where operators edit it and how upgrades or conflicting entries behave; implementation correctness cannot establish maintainer intent.

options.title: Use one canonical owner
options.body: Persist denylist policy in one owner-controlled surface and migrate or derive the other path to avoid two sources of truth.

options.title: Approve dual ownership
options.body: Keep both surfaces only with explicit maintainer-approved editing, conflict, migration, and support semantics.

recommendation.title: Use one canonical owner
recommendation.body: Persist denylist policy in one owner-controlled surface and migrate or derive the other path to avoid two sources of truth.

likelyOwner.reason: The discussion repeatedly routes the host exec security contract to steipete, who also introduced the adjacent bound-command authorization flow.
